**Verdict: REVISE**
**Blocker tags:** substantive

## Methodology lens

- **(a) Premise — PASS.** The Bash tool schema caps `timeout` at 600000 ms ("up to 600000ms / 10 minutes") with NO background exemption, and #1893's empirical signature (bg gate killed at ~10 min, exit 144, rc file missing) corroborates that the cap binds `run_in_background=true` shells. The plan's §8 verification of this assumption is correct. The motivating claim stands: the Step 9c gate (61-file workflow-invariant set, median ~18 min, max ~38 min per #1646) can never fit the cap.
- **(b) Setsid shape — BLOCKER (fix-breaking).** The canonical § Detached recipe (SKILL.md line 7043) is battle-tested, but the plan's concrete §4a launcher BREAKS it. The block splices the rc-write with a bare `;` inside the capture: `... 2>&1 ; echo \$? > /tmp/step9c-rc-issue-<N> & echo \$!`. Shell grammar parses this as three units: [pytest, FOREGROUND, all redirections bound to it] `;` [rc-write, backgrounded by the `&`] `;` [echo $!]. Consequences: (1) pytest runs foreground inside the inner shell, so the `PYTEST_PID=$( )` command substitution blocks for the full pytest wall and the Bash tool call is STILL killed at 600 s — the exact failure the plan exists to fix; (2) `\$!` captures the backgrounded rc-write's pid, not pytest's; (3) the rc file is written by a racing child before pytest exits — a garbage rc. This is verbatim the § Harvest NEVER-splice failure mode (SKILL.md ~7108-7111: splicing `&&`/`;` into the template binds setsid/nohup to the first command and the trailing `&` to the second — "detachment silently breaks"). All five §4a-4e sites inherit the same defect. **Fix:** wrap workload + rc-write as ONE detached unit per § Harvest self-harvest chaining: `PYTEST_PID=$(bash -c "setsid nohup bash -c '<timeout+env+pytest cmd> ; echo \$? > /tmp/step9c-rc-issue-<N>' < /dev/null > /tmp/step9c-pytest-issue-<N>.log 2>&1 & echo \$!")`. — grounding: plan §4a core replacement block (quoted above); SKILL.md § Harvest contract ~7104-7117 — mechanizable: yes (pin test asserts the inner `bash -c '... ; echo $? >' ` wrapping and rejects a top-level `; echo \$?` splice between `2>&1` and `&` in each launch region).
- **(c) Site enumeration — PASS.** `grep -n 'run_in_background=true' SKILL.md` → 14 hits. The plan's 5 sites (9c 1b ~9957/10079, 1c ~10164, 1d compare ~10220, 10d forms (i)/(ii) ~11723/11750, 10d form (iii) ~13794) are the complete gate-class set. Remaining hits: 8091 = inline payload lint gate (minutes-scale, correctly untouched); 4754/4760 = experimenter `poll_pipeline.py` dispatch (bounded poll chain by design); 2897/4517/7405/8587 = generic/descriptive prose. No missed site carries the gate's wall.
- **(d) Pin test — REVISE item.** `tests/test_issue_skill_step9c_compare_background.py` extracts a single 8000-char region anchored at "Classify failures against the known-red-on-main" — the 1d compare site only. That window cannot reach 1b (~line 9957), 1c (~10164), or the 10d blocks (~11750, ~13794). Plan §4f describes compare-region assertion updates only, while §6 Durability claims the test is "extended in this diff to cover all five modified launch sites" — internally inconsistent, and as written the detached shape is durably pinned at 1 of 5 sites. **Fix:** per-site region extraction (5 anchors, one per launch site), each asserting the setsid launcher + pid capture + rc-file (+ the item-(b) no-splice shape), making §6's claim true. — grounding: test file lines 12-24 vs plan §4f/§6 — mechanizable: yes (that IS the test).
- **(e) End-the-turn pairing — PASS.** The plan names the sanctioned waits (Monitor until-loop keyed on the single-flight probe; `/issue-tick <N>` cron re-wake) and explicitly bans the repeated `TaskOutput(block=true, timeout=600000)` poll chain, citing #1984 (×3 polls, ~31 min held turn).
- **(f) Choom race + breadcrumb — REVISE item (recipe deviation, not fix-breaking).** The plan's inline comment dismisses the bounded choom retry ("real python3 child is spawned immediately by uv run"; "children inherit"), but § Detached's own incident record contradicts it: #1315 observed choom on the launch pid NOT sticking to the python3 child `uv run` forked moments later (a child forked before the parent's adjustment lands inherits nothing), and SKILL.md 7150-7158 makes the ONE bounded retry (re-sweep when the real python3 child appears, or after ≤~30-60 s) "now the default rather than an option". pytest under earlyoom's `--prefer '(^|/)(pytest|python3?)'` (+300 badness) on the shared VM is exactly the protected class. Also: the plan's breadcrumb (`pid= log= rc= choom=`) omits the REQUIRED `harvest=` token (§ Harvest contract; the junit xml path serves). **Fix:** restore the one bounded choom re-sweep per SKILL.md 7150-7158 and add `harvest=/tmp/step9c-junit-issue-<N>.xml` to the breadcrumb line. — grounding: plan §4a comment vs SKILL.md 7150-7158 (#1315) + ~7104 (`harvest=` REQUIRED) — mechanizable: yes (pin test asserts `harvest=` in each breadcrumb line; retry presence greppable).
- Minor (no action forced): the plan uses `>` truncate where the canonical launcher uses `>>` append — acceptable for per-issue tmp logs that the recipe `rm -f`s at launch; fine as an allowed deviation if stated.

## Alternatives lens

- **(a) Extend the bg-Bash timeout instead? NO.** 600000 ms is the schema hard cap (`max 600000`); there is no larger value to pass. The brief's pre-answer is confirmed.
- **(b) Smaller test selection to fit 10 min? NO.** The Step 9c selection always bundles the 61-file workflow-invariant set (median ~18 min, max ~38 min, #1646); a sub-10-min gate selection does not exist without weakening the gate itself, which is out of scope for this fix.
- **(c) External orchestrator (poll_pipeline-style) instead of inline setsid? Plan's choice is right.** The § Detached recipe is repo-canonical (#833 lineage) and reuse-first; the gate needs only launch-detach + rc-file read + a sanctioned wait, and an external orchestrator adds a moving part (registration, crash-recovery of the watcher) for no coverage gain. The simplest correct alternative is exactly what the plan proposes — once item (b)'s splice is fixed.

## Recommendation

REVISE — three concrete fixes, then advance to implementer:
1. **Restructure all 5 launch blocks** to the § Harvest self-harvest chaining shape: `setsid nohup bash -c '<workload> ; echo $? > <rc-file>' < /dev/null > <log> 2>&1 & echo $!` inside the outer `bash -c` pid-capture wrapper. The current `... 2>&1 ; echo \$? > rc & echo \$!` splice runs pytest FOREGROUND inside the `$( )` capture — the fix as written does not detach and still dies at the 600 s cap.
2. **Extend the pin test to all 5 sites** (per-site anchored regions asserting setsid + pid capture + rc-file + no top-level `;`-splice), so §6's durability claim is true rather than 1-of-5.
3. **Restore the bounded choom re-sweep** (SKILL.md 7150-7158, #1315 — the uv-run→python3 fork gap is the observed incident, not a hypothetical) and add the REQUIRED `harvest=` token to each breadcrumb.

## Issues Found

### Critical (block merge)

- `SKILL.md:10123` (1b) and `SKILL.md:10247` (1c): **`\$S9C_BASETEMP` defers expansion to the detached inner shell, but `S9C_BASETEMP` is never exported — the inner shell expands it EMPTY, so pytest receives `--basetemp=/p`.**
  - Evidence: preamble `SKILL.md:10096-10099` assigns `S9C_BASETEMP=$(mktemp -d ...)` with NO `export` (only `TMPDIR` is exported). The `${S9C_BASETEMP:+...}` guard fires at the OUTER level (var set there), but the payload `\$S9C_BASETEMP` reaches the inner `bash -c` as a literal `$S9C_BASETEMP`, which the inner shell — a grandchild process that does not inherit unexported vars — expands to empty.
  - Empirically reproduced with the diff's exact quoting: unexported var → workload received `--basetemp=/p`; exported var or the plan's unescaped form → correct path. Then `uv run pytest --basetemp=/p` on a 2-test file: `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/p'` → every `tmp_path`-using test ERRORs. The workflow-invariant gate set is tmp_path-heavy, so on the VM (data disk present → `S9C_TMPROOT` non-empty → the `:+` guard always fires) EVERY Step 9c 1b/1c gate run would spew spurious errors not on the known-red ledger → compare classifies NEW → gate FAILs every round. It also silently defeats the #1408 basetemp routing this snippet exists for.
  - Round-introduced: the OLD inline shape expanded `$S9C_BASETEMP` in the same shell that set it (worked unexported); the round moved the expansion two process levels down. Note the plan §4a sketch itself used the UNESCAPED form `${S9C_BASETEMP:+--basetemp=$S9C_BASETEMP/p}` — the `\$` was an implementation-time deviation under §7 flexibility.
  - Fix (simplest): delete the backslash at both sites — outer-level expansion embeds the literal mktemp path (no quotes/spaces in mktemp paths) into the inner script, exactly the plan's form. (Alternative: `export S9C_BASETEMP` at 10098/10235 — either works; pick one.) Also fix the `test_step9c_baseline.py` docstring that rationalizes the deferral (see Minor m1).
